10.need-data: Load your data above: the card and the drift reference are verified against it.

reads.title: What this stage does
reads.body: It builds the model card from what the notebook already recorded in stages 1 to 9: nothing is recomputed and the test set isn't opened again. Here you name who answers for it and, depending on your decision, the monitoring plan or what would have to change.

decision.title: Your stage 9 decision
decision.usar: Use it: the card carries a monitoring plan.
decision.iterar: Iterate: the card spells out what to change. This test set was already opened and doesn't count as new.
decision.no-usar: Don't use it: the card spells out why and what would have to change. It's a valid result.

owner.title: Who answers for it
owner.label: Person or role that answers for this model
owner.help: With a name: a person or a role (for example, «Head of retention»). The card labels it as written by you. Up to {max} characters.

not-use.label: What NOT to use it for (optional)
not-use.help: In your own words: uses this card doesn't back, besides the ones that come from the notebook. Up to {max} characters.

cadence.title: How often it's retrained
cadence.label: Retrain every (months)
cadence.help-time: Your test backs {sugerida} months: from the stage 6 cut ({corte}) to the last date in your data ({fin}). You can shorten it; lengthening it asks for your reason.
cadence.help-no-time: Your test wasn't split by time, so it doesn't say how long the model holds: you write the cadence, in whole months from 1 to {max}.
cadence.reason-label: Your reason to retrain less often
cadence.reason-help: Required: your test backs {sugerida} months and you wrote more. Up to {max} characters.

change.title: What would have to change
change.label-no-usar: What would have to change for it to serve
change.help-no-usar: In your own words: more data, another decision, another column… It stays on the card as written by you. Up to {max} characters.
change.label-iterar: What you'll change before testing again
change.help-iterar: In your own words. This test set was already opened: to come back you need a different split for it to count as new. Up to {max} characters.

text.title: Text columns: which ones to watch
text.help: To compare a new CSV with today's, the reference keeps, for each column you tick, the name of its categories with {min} rows or more (up to {max}) and how many rows each has. It stays in your browser, and travels in the notebook file only if you export it. For the ones you don't tick, no name is kept and the check doesn't watch them. Numbers aren't touched: they're kept as rounded ranges, never rows.
text.status: Ticked: {n} of {total}. The rest are neither kept nor watched.

plan.title: Monitoring plan
plan.body: Drift is watched on {columnas} model columns against {n} rows of the sealed training set. The reference keeps only aggregates (cuts and frequencies; for text columns, only the ones you ticked, with their category names), never rows.
plan.thresholds: A moderate change from a PSI of {moderada} and an alert from {alerta}: stage 4 conventions, not a test.
plan.inputs: This measures inputs, not performance: to watch performance, save the winner as a file (below) and use it in Probeta with new rows that carry the real result.
plan.none: The drift reference couldn't be built with this data: without it, the card isn't complete.

preview.note: It's built from what the notebook already recorded and what you write here; it's recorded when you save the stage.

constancia.title: Your model card
constancia.body: It comes out of the notebook: if you correct a stage, the card is rebuilt. Download it to share it; the file is born and stays on your machine.
constancia.fail: The card couldn't be built: some evidence is missing from the notebook.

drift.title: Check whether your data changed
drift.intro: Load a new CSV with the model's columns and compare it with this card's reference. It measures whether today's inputs look like the training ones; it does not measure whether the model is still right: for that, save the winner (below) and use it in Probeta with new rows that carry the real result. The file is not stored and does not leave your browser.
drift.no-reference: This card has no readable reference: record the stage again.
drift.missing: The file lacks model columns: {columnas}. Without them it can't be compared.

verdict.sigue: Keep going: no column changed appreciably.
verdict.revisar: Review: some column changed a little, couldn't be measured or changed type. Look at which one before trusting the predictions.
verdict.reentrenar: Retrain: some column moved far from what the model saw.

drift.reminder: Remember: this measures inputs, not the model's performance.
drift.unwatched: Not watched by your choice ({columnas}): {lista}. The verdict above says nothing about those columns.

field.no_usar_para: What not to use it for (written by you)
field.razon_cadencia: Your reason to lengthen the cadence
field.vigilar_texto: Text columns you watch (chosen by you)

sheet.title: Model card
sheet.intro: Card built by Probeta DS from what the notebook recorded: nothing was recomputed and the test set wasn't opened again. Each line says which stage, date and fingerprint it comes from; what's derived isn't edited and what the owner wrote is labeled.
sheet.privacy: It carries no rows: it carries counts, costs, column names and names of categories with support, quantile cuts and what the owner wrote.

section.limites: Limits and what NOT to use it for

source.owner-pending: Written by the owner · recorded with this stage

datos.modelo: Model chosen: {ganador}, by cross-validation inside the training set.
datos.columnas: Columns that go into the model: {usar}. Left out: {excluir}.

poblacion.sin-exclusiones: Nobody was excluded from that population.
poblacion.periodo: Period of the data: from {desde} to {hasta}.
poblacion.sin-periodo: The data carries no date: the period it covers can't be stated.
poblacion.fuera: Rows outside the split (no target, no date, no unit or from units in the test set): {fuera}.

metricas.costo: Model cost on the test set: {costo100} per 100 decisions (from {bajo100} to {alto100}).
metricas.regla: Your rule of today: {regla100} per 100 decisions.
metricas.metrica: {metrica}: {seleccion} when choosing the model and {enPrueba} on the test set.
metricas.segmentos: Segments with enough support to be measured: {conSoporte} of {total}.
metricas.peor-sin-soporte: No segment has enough support to point out the worst.
metricas.peor-ninguno: No segment with support costs more than the whole test set.

decision.decision-iterar: Decision: iterate before deciding. Your reason: «{razon}».
decision.decision-no-usar: Decision: don't use it. Your reason: «{razon}».
decision.costo: The model costs {modelo100} per 100 decisions; today's way ({hoy}), {hoy100}.
decision.umbral: It acts at threshold {umbral}, the one from your costs: {alertas100} alerts per 100 cases and {falsas100} false alarms per 100 alerts.
decision.umbral-movido: It acts at threshold {umbral}, chosen while looking at the test set (optimistic): {alertas100} alerts per 100 cases and {falsas100} false alarms per 100 alerts.
decision.clase: With no probabilities, it decides with the class it predicts: {alertas100} alerts per 100 cases and {falsas100} false alarms per 100 alerts.
decision.capacidad: Your team handles {capacidad} out of every 100 cases.

limites.predice: It's for predicting, not explaining: what the model associates isn't what causes.
limites.poblacion: Only for this population: {poblacion}. For any other there's no test that backs it.
limites.periodo: It was tested with data from {desde} to {hasta}: outside that period there's no test that backs it.
limites.sin-soporte: Segments without enough rows to be measured (how it does there is unknown): {segmentos}.
limites.prueba-chica: The test set had only {filas} rows: a handful of cases moves the figures.
limites.reabierta: The test set was opened with {aperturas} different setups: its figures are no longer unbiased.
limites.patron: Where it fails, in your own words (stage 8): {texto}
limites.poco-fiable: What the model said and what happened drifted {brechaPct} percentage points apart in one bin: the threshold from your costs is unreliable.
limites.umbral-optimista: Threshold {umbral} was chosen while looking at the test set: its figures are optimistic.
limites.dueno: What NOT to use it for (written by the owner): {texto}

cumplio.fuga: Data leakage checked: {alertas} columns with an alert; {usar} columns go in and {excluir} were excluded.
cumplio.particion: {esquema} split with a sealed test set (seal {sello}): {entrenamiento} rows to train and {prueba} to test, with no overlap.
cumplio.linea-base: Baseline: the best candidate ({base}) costs {base100} per 100 decisions.
cumplio.supera: Beats the baseline: {media100} less per 100 decisions (from {bajo100} to {alto100}).
cumplio.no-supera: Doesn't beat the baseline ({media100} per 100 decisions; from {bajo100} to {alto100}). It's written down.
cumplio.senal: Has signal: the permutation test gives p = {p} with {n} permutations.
cumplio.sin-senal: No clear signal: the permutation test gives p = {p} with {n} permutations.
cumplio.incertidumbre: Uncertainty measured: on the test set the cost runs from {bajo100} to {alto100} per 100 decisions.
cumplio.calibracion: Calibration measured: Brier {brier} against {brierBase} for always saying the base rate.
cumplio.calibracion-sin-probabilidades: Calibration: couldn't be measured, the winner gives no probabilities.
cumplio.calibracion-no-aplica: Calibration: doesn't apply when estimating a quantity.
cumplio.robustez: Robustness measured (stage 8): with {nivel} % noise in the numbers, {metrica} goes from {de} to {a} and still beats its best rival without a model ({rivalNombre}: {rival}).
cumplio.robustez-cae: Robustness (stage 8): with {nivel} % noise in the numbers, {metrica} goes from {de} to {a} and stops beating its best rival without a model ({rivalNombre}: {rival}). It is on the record.
cumplio.robustez-ya-perdia: Robustness (stage 8): noise is not the cause; before adding it, {metrica} ({de}) already did not beat its best rival without a model ({rivalNombre}: {rival}).
cumplio.robustez-sin-medir: Robustness: not measured. The stage 8 stress test is optional and was not run on this opening of the test.

vigilancia.sin-vigilar: Not watched by the owner's choice ({columnas}): {lista}. If they change, this plan won't notice.
vigilancia.umbrales: Drift thresholds (PSI): moderate from {moderada}, alert from {alerta}. They're conventions, not a test.
vigilancia.solo-entradas: This plan measures whether today's inputs look like the training ones. It doesn't measure performance: for that, save the winner as a file in this stage and use it in Probeta with new rows that carry the real result.
vigilancia.piso: Floor of the decision: stop using it if the model stops costing less than today's way ({hoy}): now {modelo100} against {hoy100} per 100 decisions.
vigilancia.piso-beneficio: In net benefit per 100 decisions the model gives {beneficio100} and today's way {hoy100}: if it drops to today's, stop using it.
vigilancia.cadencia-sin-tiempo: Retraining cadence (in months): {cadencia}. The owner wrote it: the test wasn't split by time and doesn't say how long the model holds.
vigilancia.cadencia-alargada: Retraining cadence (in months): {cadencia}, longer than the {sugerida} the test supports. Owner's reason: «{razon}».
vigilancia.cadencia-acortada: Retraining cadence (in months): {cadencia}, shorter than the {sugerida} the test supports (the owner's decision).
vigilancia.cadencia: Retraining cadence (in months): {cadencia}, the one the test supports.

variante.que-cambiaria: What would have to change for it to serve (written by the owner): {texto}
variante.que-cambiar: What to change before testing again (written by the owner): {texto}
variante.prueba-gastada: The test set was already opened ({aperturas}): if the model is improved, that test set doesn't count as new; a different split is needed.

model.title: Take the winner with you
model.body: Save the winner as a «.probeta.json» file to score new rows and watch its performance in Probeta («Load saved model»). It is fitted again with the training rows —the test is not opened— and the file carries the model, not your rows.
model.contains: The file carries the model with the ranges and categories it saw in training, plus the name of your file, the fingerprint of the data, the seal of the split, the row counts and the library versions; no rows.
model.contains-knn: This winner is nearest neighbours: the file carries the training rows (that is how this model works). Save it only where your data may be.
model.need-data: Load the file you worked with above: the model is fitted with its training rows and the fingerprint confirms it is the same one.
model.other-file: This is not the file you used: the partition seal does not match, so the model is not fitted.
model.working: Fitting the winner with the training rows… The test is not opened.
model.error: The model could not be saved ({motivo}). Try again.

reglas.title: The winner's rules
reglas.body: A tree of a few questions about the model's columns that copies what the winner decides on the rows you upload, so you can take it to a system where Python does not run (text and SQL). Pick a CSV with rows shaped like your data: the winner is refitted with the training rows, and the tree is built with yours.
reglas.never-truth: Here the rules are never measured against the truth: the test was opened once in stage 8 and is not opened again. The target column, if your file has one, does not leave your browser and is not used: only the columns the model reads travel.
reglas.need-data: Load the file you worked with above: the winner is fitted with its training rows and the fingerprint confirms it is the same one.
reglas.other-file: This is not the file you used: the partition seal does not match, so the winner is not fitted.
reglas.working: Fitting the winner and building the tree with your rows… The test is not opened.
reglas.csv: The file could not be read as a CSV ({motivo}).
reglas.missing: The file is missing columns the model reads: {columnas}.
reglas.too-few: With so few rows there is no tree worth building: at least {min} are needed.
reglas.error: The rules could not be built ({motivo}). Try again.
reglas.sin-verdad: The rules were measured against what the winner decides on rows the tree did not see, not against the truth: the test was already opened once and is not opened again.
reglas.from-file: Rules built with the rows of “{nombre}”.
